pages.title: What it does
text: It is a multiplier: a stat value of v means an experience multiplier of m = 1 + v / 100. So v = 100 is double experience.
It is applied exactly once, in the single booking function, and covers kills, first-time rewards (mining / crafting / smelting / fishing / trading) and experience crystals.
Because there is only one booking site, double-counting (paying a multiplier twice for one action) is structurally impossible.

pages.title: Flat (numeric) line
text: The curve is LINEAR: +1.666667 percentage points per point.
The old curve, gain = 100 * x / (x + 60), had an initial slope of 100/60 = 1.666667, so the early feel is unchanged.

pages.title: Percent line
text: Also LINEAR: 5.0 per point, on the DESIGN_BASELINE basis with reference B_ref = 50 percentage points.
Contribution = 50 * gain / 100, i.e. +2.5 percentage points per point. 20 points -> +50.00; 50 -> +125.00; 100 -> +250.00; 200 -> +500.00.
The two contributions add up to the stat value v, and the final multiplier is m = 1 + v/100.

pages.title: Ceiling & returns
text: Both lines are linear, so the experience multiplier keeps climbing until it meets the attribute's own range (1.0E6, unreachable in practice). There is no designed ceiling and no diminishing returns.

There is also an optional global budget, xp.minute_cap (0 by default, meaning disabled; 3000 is recommended for servers): at most that much experience is booked inside a rolling 60 second window, and the rest is discarded.
That budget, not the multiplier number, is what really paces the game.

pages.title: Practical advice
text: This is a compounding stat: the earlier you invest, the more every later point of experience is worth.
Pair it with experience crystals to rush the early levels. Server admins should look at xp.minute_cap before combining a high multiplier with automation.
